statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 5% (low) on the closed-venue floor, Stress 53% (elevated), Confidence 85% (high).
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the mapped state stays EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The only published danger window is the 22:00-00:00 UTC futures reopening, where the forecast carries a WATCH allowance against an unobserved weekend auction.
headline: Nasdaq-100 unquoted at 29,544.16 with about fifteen hours of the CME weekend halt remaining; the IRGC Hormuz claim has stood unconfirmed for roughly three and a half hours, easing Stress to 53% while Tail holds the closed-venue floor
body:
The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.16, up about 62 points or 0.21% from a 29,482.30 previous close, after ranging between 29,440.15 and 29,655.22. Price retraced repeatedly in both directions inside that 215-point range, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure that the Tail score measures. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the Friday 21:00 UTC settle and are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on 6 September. That reopening hour and the first full hour after it are the two WATCH slots of this forecast.

The geopolitical sequence produced no new verified step during the current hour. The most recent development remains the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps statement carried at about 03:03 UTC, saying its naval force struck an American unmanned surface vessel attempting to enter what it described as a restricted area of the Strait of Hormuz. That claim has now stood for roughly three and a half hours with no CENTCOM confirmation or denial and no corroborating report, which eases Stress one point to 53%. It follows Saturday's exchange, in which US Central Command said it had disabled two Iranian crude tankers and destroyed a third after Iranian ballistic missiles were fired at two US warships, and the IRGC counter-claim of attacks on three tankers and three US-linked vessels.

Cross-asset evidence is Friday-dated and calm relative to the conflict. VIX closed at 14.53, the 2-year Treasury yield stood at 4.34% and the 10-year at 4.77% on the latest H.15 observation, and WTI settled near $91.48 with Brent near $96.28 after a weekly crude gain above 9% driven by Hormuz supply risk. The macro impulse into the halt was hawkish: August nonfarm payrolls rose 162,000 against expectations near 53,000, with the unemployment rate at 4.1% and average hourly earnings up 3.1% year on year. The Federal Reserve blackout ahead of the 15-16 September FOMC began on 5 September, so no Fed speakers can add to that impulse before PPI on 10 September and CPI on 11 September.

Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is held at the 5% closed-venue floor because the pathological price path it measures cannot exist while the venue is shut, and Stress at 53% carries the unresolved chokepoint conflict, the energy premium and a two-day information gap that must clear through a single weekend auction. Confidence is 85%: current verified levels, yields, oil, volatility and calendar coverage are held, but no live Nasdaq-100 price path exists in any hour of the halt. The shared Finviz cross-asset context was about five hours old at assessment time and therefore outside its freshness window, so it was not used as evidence and the assessment rests on independent primary-source research.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours run from 06:00 UTC on 5 September to 05:00 UTC on 6 September and lie entirely inside the CME weekend halt. All 24 slots are available from published Claude assessments, every one is scored at the closed-venue Tail floor of 4-5% under a normal mode, and every one maps to EA_ON and green. Stress was flat at 38% from 06:00 UTC through 10:00 UTC, climbed from 39% at 11:00 UTC to 42% by 14:00 UTC as the Saturday US-Iran sequence developed, stepped to 48% at 15:00 UTC once the CENTCOM tanker strikes were verified, rose to 52% by 19:00 UTC and peaked at 57% at 20:00 UTC when the IRGC counter-claim and Iran's threat of more severe attacks were published. It then eased to 53% by 02:00 UTC as the sequence went quiet, lifted to 56% at 03:00 UTC on the newly published IRGC unmanned-vessel claim and eased again to 55% and 54% as that claim went unconfirmed. Confidence held in a narrow 85-86% band throughout: the assessment kept current verified levels, yields, oil, volatility and calendar coverage, but no live Nasdaq-100 price path existed in any of the 24 hours.
outlookSummary: Sixteen of the twenty-four published hours fall inside the CME weekend halt, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in them; the mapped policy state stays EA_ON with Tail on the 5% closed-venue floor through the dormant hours, lifting from 13:00 UTC as a conditional pre-auction gap allowance and peaking at 14% in the last full hour of the halt. The final eight slots are different: futures are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on 6 September, so those hours are the first in which structure can exist. The reopening hour and the first full hour after it each carry a 20% Tail allowance, map to WATCH and yellow, and together form the only published danger window; the last six slots step back to 17%, 15%, 14%, 13%, 12% and 12% and to green on the assumption of an orderly auction into the shortened US Labor Day futures session. Stress opens at 53%, holds a 52% low in the quiet Sunday hours, then rebuilds through the afternoon to a 71% peak at the reopen before easing to 60%. Confidence declines from 85% to 72% because every later slot rests on Friday-dated market evidence and on a geopolitical sequence whose latest step is still an unconfirmed IRGC claim.
